'''Angela Susan Roberts'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201125_039660000/event|title = Speech – New Zealand Parliament}}</ref> is a New Zealand teacher, unionist and politician.

==Early life and career==
Roberts spent 20 years in the education sector teaching economics and drama, including at [[Stratford High School, New Zealand|Stratford High School]].<ref name=stranglehold>{{cite news |last1=Coster |first1=Deena |title=Candidate's bid to break National's stranglehold in Taranaki-King Country |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/122148211/election-2020-candidates-bid-to-break-nationals-stranglehold-in-taranakiking-country |access-date=6 August 2020 |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=23 July 2020 }}</ref> She was president of the [[Post Primary Teachers' Association]] (PPTA) union from 2013 to 2017. In that role, she was critical of then-[[Minister of Education (New Zealand)|Minister of Education]] [[Hekia Parata]] on teaching issues including [[Novopay]] and [[Charter schools in New Zealand|charter schools]]. When she returned to teaching in 2017, she became senior vice president of the PPTA.<ref name='run for Labour'>{{cite news |last1=Moir |first1=Jo |title=Former PPTA president Angela Roberts to run for Labour |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/417455/former-ppta-president-angela-roberts-to-run-for-labour |access-date=6 August 2020 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=25 May 2020 }}</ref>

Roberts was involved in the Just Transition Summit conversations in [[Taranaki]], following the [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|Sixth Labour Government]]'s 2018 decision to ban new offshore oil and gas exploration permits. She took a particular interest in the role of education and training in sustaining future businesses and workforce.<ref name='run for Labour'/>

==Member of Parliament==

There was speculation Roberts would run as a [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] candidate in the 2017 election, a notion she did not rule out. However, at the last minute, she decided against running.<ref name='run for Labour'/>

Roberts entered Parliament in the {{NZ election link|2020}}. She ran for the electorate of {{NZ electorate link|Taranaki-King Country}}, coming second behind the incumbent [[New Zealand National Party|National]] MP [[Barbara Kuriger]] by a margin of 3,134 votes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Taranaki-King Country – Official Count|url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-50.html|access-date=9 November 2020|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref> The Labour Party performed strongly and Roberts was elected to Parliament as a list MP, ranked 50th on the [[party list]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Coughlan, Thomas |title=Ayesha Verrall leads fresh-faced Labour party list for 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/300034942/ayesha-verrall-leads-freshfaced-labour-party-list-for-2020 |access-date=15 June 2020 |date=15 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020074743/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/300034942/ayesha-verrall-leads-freshfaced-labour-party-list-for-2020|archive-date=20 October 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result Successful Candidates |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=5 February 2021 }}</ref>

Roberts gave her maiden statement on 2 December 2020.<ref name="f8942">{{cite web |title=Address In Reply Debate |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201202_052080000/mallard-trevor-roberts-angela/ |access-date=11 June 2025 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref> She was a member of the education committee from 2 December 2020 until 8 September 2023, a member of the primary production committee from 4 May 2022 to 16 February 2023, and deputy chair of the primary production committee from 16 February to 8 September 2023.<ref name="f894">{{cite web |title=Roberts, Angela |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/roberts-angela/ |access-date=11 June 2025 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref>

On 29 September 2023, Roberts was physically assaulted at a [[Surgery (politics)|surgery]] at the [[Rotary International|Rotary club]] in [[Inglewood, New Zealand|Inglewood]], [[Taranaki]], while canvassing for Taranaki-King Country. The man reportedly confronted Roberts before he “grabbed [her] shoulders" and shook her violently "in order to emphasise the point he was making" before slapping her across the face.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mathias |first=Shanti |date=2023-09-29 |title=Labour candidate slapped following debate in Taranaki |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/live-updates/29-09-2023/labour-candidate-slapped-following-debate-in-taranaki |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=The Spinoff |language=en}}</ref> Roberts later said to [[Radio New Zealand]] "It feels like, incrementally, there is a growing acceptance of aggression in politics and our democratic processes. This must change." She thanked National MP Barbara Kuriger for reaching out to her after the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 September 2023 |title='Completely unacceptable': Labour candidate Angela Roberts 'slapped' following political debate |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/499039/completely-unacceptable-labour-candidate-angela-roberts-slapped-following-political-debate |access-date=29 September 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |language=en-nz}}</ref>

During the [[2023 New Zealand general election]] held on 14 October, Roberts contested Taranaki-King Country a second time. She lost to incumbent Kuriger by a margin of 14,355 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Taranaki-King Country - Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-50.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=16 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210215713/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-50.html |archive-date=10 December 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>
